summary: Applies a smooth procedural noise field to POP attributes. By default it moves every point's P attribute through X, Y, and Z, but it can also output raw Noise, NoiseGradient, NoiseCurl, and mapped per-point parameter variations.

key_params.name: noiselookupattrib
key_params.note: Point input attribute used to compute noise lookup position.

key_params.name: type
key_params.note: Perlin or Simplex noise in 2D, 3D, or 4D.

key_params.name: noisesize
key_params.note: Number of noise components to compute.

key_params.name: offset
key_params.note: Offset added to resulting noise values.

key_params.name: attrclass
key_params.note: Point, vertex, or primitive attribute class.

key_params.name: group
key_params.note: Restrict operation to a named group.

key_params.name: s
key_params.note: Scale source geometry in noise space.

key_params.name: t4d
key_params.note: Translate through the fourth noise dimension.

key_params.name: combineop
key_params.note: How computed values combine with an attribute.

key_params.name: combineentity
key_params.note: Noise, Curl 3D, or Curl 2D source for combine operation.

key_params.name: computenormals
key_params.note: Compute point normals after the operation.

key_params.name: map0element
key_params.note: Attribute or component mapped to a parameter.

key_params.name: map0parm
key_params.note: Target parameter mapped from the attribute.

key_params.name: map0combineop
key_params.note: Set, multiply, or add mapped attribute value.

common_gotchas: By default Noise POP applies the field to the P attribute, so validate POP bounds after adding noise motion.
Animate noise by changing Translate or Translate 4D, for example with absTime.seconds, rather than by inventing a separate time parameter.
The Map page supports per-point parameter overrides for amp, offset, exp, period, spread, and gain; use it when every point needs different noise controls.
Raw Noise is scalar by default; set Noise Size and Parameter Size deliberately before expecting vector attributes.
Use official amp for amplitude; amplitude is a display concept, not the internal parameter name.
